National Assembly
Twenty-First Session
Complete Minutes
Proceedings
23
2083 Ashadh
Wednesday
Meeting Number - 26
The National Assembly's meeting today commenced at 12:27 PM under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson, Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members, the proceedings of today's National Assembly meeting (12:27 PM) begin. Honourable members, names have been received to speak during the Zero Hour. I have allocated one minute each for speaking during the Zero Hour. First, Honourable Member Gita Devkota.
Honourable Member Gita Devkota (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, I offer my heartfelt tribute to the tragic incident that occurred in Bharatpur Metropolitan City-23 on the night of Ashadh 20th, where a wild elephant named Dhurke took the lives of a mother and son while they were sleeping at home, and I express my deep condolences to the bereaved family. Chairperson, it is said that the elephant Dhurke has already taken the lives of about 24 people, but the government still seems busy with meetings, reports, and relief announcements. If citizens are not safe even while sleeping at home, where is the state's security? Conservation of wildlife is necessary, but not at the cost of citizens' lives. Dhurke should be immediately controlled and kept in a secure quarantine or under special surveillance. The affected families should be provided with appropriate relief and justice. Effective fencing, surveillance, and safe relocation of high-risk families in settlements around Nikunj should be done immediately. The government must now provide security, not just tributes. Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Dharmendra Paswan.
Honourable Member Dharmendra Paswan (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, I wanted to say something about the government's 100 days regarding security. Instead of stopping incidents in the Madhesh, incidents have increased. Among various reasons, the accused are roaming freely. The victim Maju Sada of Supari Gadi Municipality Ward No. 3 is staying safely in a safe house in Krishna Savan Rural Municipality, while the main accused is roaming freely and has not been apprehended. Through the Chairperson, I strongly urge the government to apprehend them immediately and proceed with legal action.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Mahanta Thakur.
Honourable Member Mahanta Thakur (Loktantrik Samajwadi Party, Nepal): Honourable Chairperson, due to the destruction of the Chure-Bhawar region, water sources in the Madhesh have dried up, fields are parched, and paddy planting has not occurred. There is a scarcity of drinking water. Even hand pumps have dried up, and nothing has been done by the government so far. Thank you, Jai Madhesh.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Meenasingh Rakhal.
Honourable Member Meenasingh Rakhal (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Chairperson, how long will Karnali have to suffer? Why do we only hear news of accidents, disasters, and state neglect every day? A passenger Force vehicle going from Surkhet to Kalikot fell into the Karnali River, and the vehicle has not been found yet. The exact number of passengers is unknown. The victim families are worried. In Jumla's Hima Rural Municipality, one person died and two were injured due to lightning strikes, and many sheep died. Similarly, in Dolpa, one person lost their life in a road accident, and others are undergoing treatment. I offer my heartfelt tribute to the deceased souls and express my deep condolences to the bereaved families. I wish the injured a speedy recovery. I have a clear demand from the government: provide appropriate compensation to the families of the deceased, free and effective treatment for the injured, and give high priority to roads, rescue, and disaster management in Karnali. Karnali's citizens should not be treated as second-class citizens. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Ram Kumari Jhankri.
Honourable Member Ram Kumari Jhankri (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honourable Chairperson, I want to draw the government's attention to the news I have been seeing in recent days. This government came with the slogan of good governance. It is reported that many people in the hierarchical bureaucracy have resigned en masse, and dozens of advisors to ministers have been appointed at the level of first-class and second-class officers, receiving salaries and facilities. What is this? People who chanted the slogan of good governance will not run the administration through a hierarchical bureaucracy, and unelected individuals will rule Singha Durbar. What is this method? Through the Chairperson, I request that the concerned ministers or the Prime Minister's Office provide information to the House regarding this, and I want to inform the public. I want to know on what basis, with what decisions, and under which constitution and law they have been given this authority, and how they can do this beyond their commitments? The concerned ministers or the Prime Minister's Office should provide information to the House about this. I want to inform the public, and through you, Honourable Chairperson, I request information in writing about which decision led to this. (Time expired.)
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Rekha Kumari Jha.
Honourable Member Rekha Kumari Jha (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honourable Chairperson, today I want to draw the government's attention to some important issues directly related to the daily lives of the people: education, housing, health, and good governance. First, I want to talk about the education sector. Before coming to power, the government had pledged to control the arbitrary fees of private schools, reduce the financial burden on parents, and systematize the education sector. However, today the opposite is seen. Many private schools are not fully complying with the government's directives. They are collecting fees under other headings. Thank you, I'm done.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Roshi Mechhe.
Honourable Member Roshi Mechhe (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honourable Chairperson, on one hand, policy documents claim the country is free from load shedding, and on the other hand, the government is boasting about energy exports to neighboring markets. While keeping its own citizens in darkness, is our energy policy focused on fulfilling national needs or merely for propaganda for foreign trade? The Terai is burning with 40-degree heat, industries are shut down, and low voltage is burning refrigerators and fans in people's homes. This is not a shortage of electricity, but the extreme managerial helplessness of the Nepal Electricity Authority. What is the use of increased production when the distribution system reaching the consumer's doorstep is four decades old and dilapidated? Therefore, I want to draw the attention of the Ministry of Energy, Water Resources, and Irrigation to initiate urgent structural reforms by establishing an emergency fund for the technical upgrading of the last-mile distribution infrastructure. Citizens who pay the state's tariffs have the legal right to uninterrupted energy, which is consumer sovereignty. The tariffs paid by the people are for light, not for the state's... (Time expired.)
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Basudev Ghimire.
Honourable Member Basudev Ghimire (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, I want to condemn the atrocities, the manhandling, and the violence that the government perpetrated against the visually impaired who were protesting for their rights at Maitighar. Through you, Honourable Chairperson, I want to ask the Home Minister of Nepal if this is an excellent example of the good governance this government talks about, or an excellent example of violence. Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Samjhana Devkota.
Honourable Member Samjhana Devkota (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honourable Chairperson, it seems the Council of Ministers amended the Education Act on Ashadh 18th. It has introduced a provision that individuals with political party membership cannot serve as members and chairpersons of the School Management Committee. It is stipulated that only individuals who have not been affiliated with any political party for at least 4 years prior to the formation of the School Management Committee can be members. This curtails people's political rights. Political rights are among the major human rights issues; they are also fundamental rights. In a class society, there are class ideologies; a person without ideology cannot be imagined. It is the government's foolishness to treat politics as a criminal offense and restrict entry into the education sector. This decision of the Council of Ministers seems similar to the transfer of mayors; attention should be paid to this. Okay, thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Somnath Poudel.
Honourable Member Somnath Poudel (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honourable Chairperson, news is coming out in the media that the landless squatters kept at the hold centers in Nagarkot and Bode have been brought to chowks in various places like Koteshwor and left stranded on the roads. The government, which claimed to provide a long-term solution, bulldozed the shanties of these landless squatters without even providing prior notice, and after two and a half months of bulldozing, they have been left on the streets. I want to strongly condemn and denounce this act. The Prime Minister and ministers of the government are not listening to the cries of the landless and poor people. I think there is a problem with their hearing capacity. If they cannot hear such cries, there must be some problem with their ears. Therefore, I demand that a specialist doctor be arranged to treat the ears of the Prime Minister and ministers. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members, the Zero Hour speaking session concludes here. Honourable members, the Ministry-wise Question and Answer session will now commence. Honourable members, after the Honourable Minister responds, if the questioner Honourable member wishes, they can ask a supplementary question related to their question within 1 minute. Now, Honourable members, I would like to invite the Honourable Minister of Physical Infrastructure and Transport, Sunil Lamshal, to the rostrum to answer the questions posed by the Honourable member.
Honourable members, now I will provide time to the questioner Honourable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma to ask his question.
Honourable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, through you, Honourable Chairperson, I want to ask the Honourable Minister. Regarding the Khulalu-Hilsa section of the Karnali Corridor, specifically the Khulalu-Sallisalla and Simikot-Hilsa sections, many concrete bridges have been left abandoned since their construction began, most have not even started construction or are incomplete. What is the actual progress status of these bridges? What are the main obstacles in their construction? What steps has the government taken through contract processes and resource management to expedite the work, and by when is the entire project targeted for completion? I request clarification. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Minister.
Honourable Minister of Physical Infrastructure and Transport, Mr. Sunil Lamshal: Honourable Chairperson and Honourable members, specifically regarding this road, there are currently about 8 bridges mentioned in the details. I have not visited the site yet, but there is a program to visit the site, and this road section is also a high priority for us. Currently, a total of 9 bridges are planned to be advanced through the design and build method and 2 through contract packages. However, based on our site study, we will build all the bridges that need to be built.

Currently, the monitoring of all under-construction projects will also be rigorous. Rather than reading out the objective details here, it is better to go to the field and see. We will go to the field and identify all the problems. After solving all the problems, I reached there on the 3rd of Shrawan and resolved all the issues you raised through an on-site inspection. Since the government's agenda is to manage the budget and advance the procurement process for all the bridges in that section this year, I will provide further details after returning from there, or I will provide them here in the parliament. Thank you. - Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, as the questioning honorable member wishes to ask a supplementary question, I provide time to ask a supplementary question focused on the topic. (12:41 PM) Honorable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Nepal Communist Party): - Honorable Chairperson, through the Honorable Chairperson, I wish to ask a supplementary question to the Honorable Minister. The Karnali Corridor is not only the backbone of Karnali Province but also of the neighboring provinces in terms of trade and development. It is a tragedy that the design of five concrete bridges has not yet been approved after such a long time and that landslides in many places have not been controlled. Due to the narrow road, hundreds of Karnali residents lose their lives annually. We need to manage sufficient budget to expand and upgrade the Karnali Corridor to a two-lane road, complete it within the stipulated time by achieving 100% capital expenditure, promote tourism, and open the Hilsa-China border to improve the economic condition and living standards of the country as well as the people of Karnali. What projects and plans have been formulated for this? (...Time expired.) Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Minister. (12:43 PM) Honorable Minister of Physical Infrastructure Development Mr. Sunil Lamshal: - Honorable Chairperson, regarding the issue of Karnali and the road you raised, the government has given the highest priority to structures like the ones you mentioned. The goal is to complete the conversion of all single-lane roads to double lanes within three years. There is sufficient budget for this, and we will start the work by preparing DPRs and estimates in this fiscal year. The road section you mentioned, along with roads connecting all district headquarters and all local level headquarters, will be tendered this year. All of them. Whichever is in Mugu district or any local level center in Karnali Province that does not have road access, or has a dirt road, or an unsafe road. We have allocated sufficient budget this year for double lanes to local level centers and double lanes to all district headquarters. Due to excessive accidents and many deaths occurring there, we have advanced this program to end such incidents permanently. Regarding landslides, we have also managed a special budget and will complete all identified landslides within the next three years, and we will immediately tender all studies conducted this year and conduct studies for those yet to be studied and then tender them. We have also prepared DPRs for that. We will definitely solve the problem you mentioned in this section, and we are also working on the other border. Since this is also a tourist road, we will advance this work with special priority, and I believe we will build roads up to the China border. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: - Now I request the Honorable Minister to take his seat. Honorable members, I invite the Honorable Minister of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Ms. Gauri Kumari, to the rostrum to answer the questions posed by the honorable member. Honorable members, now I provide time to the questioning honorable member, Mr. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima", to ask her question. Honorable Mr. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Nepal Communist Party): (12:45 PM) Honorable Chairperson, first of all, I would like to extend my sincere thanks to the Honorable Minister through the Honorable Chairperson for being present in this meeting of the National Assembly to answer questions while fulfilling his responsibilities. My question is as follows: According to the price analysis report 2083 published by the Department of Commerce, Supply and Consumer Protection, there have been excessive fluctuations in the prices of food items. Nepal Oil Corporation has increased the price of petroleum products six times in the months of Chaitra and Baishakh alone. The increase in fuel prices has made transportation fares more expensive, directly impacting the prices of food and consumer goods, while the increase in aviation fuel prices has led to an increase in domestic airfares. This has not only burdened the poor by breaking their backs but has also pushed the overall economy towards inflation. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Minister. (12:46 PM) Honorable Minister of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Ms. Gauri Kumari: - Honorable Chairperson, greetings to all honorable members. I express my gratitude for the interest shown in the activities of the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies and for the suggestions and queries raised. Thank you for providing me with time to present the answer in the esteemed house. I wish to present the answer to the question raised by the honorable member Madan Kumari Shah Garima. The Department of Commerce, Supply and Consumer Protection has been publishing a monthly price analysis report by collecting data through on-site inspections of various five commercial offices under the department, including the Kalimati Fruits and Vegetables Market Development Committee, Nepal Food Kirana Business Association, Nepal Retailers Association, Nepal Oil Corporation, and the Department of Nepal Rastra Bank, as well as from various sources. In this context, according to the price analysis report for Baishakh 2082/083 published through the department's website, fluctuations have mainly occurred in the prices of local ghee, beans, cowpeas, bottle gourd, green beans, cucumbers, and other vegetables. The report concludes that the unnatural fluctuation in vegetable and fruit prices from farmer to consumer within a month is influenced by the increase in petroleum prices, the state of vegetable production, and intermediaries according to market levels. Nepal Oil Corporation regularly adjusts petroleum product prices through an automated system. Despite the recent difficult situation in the Middle East, facilitation is being provided in the management of petroleum product supply. Along with this, to maintain market price transparency, control unnatural price increases, prevent artificial shortages, and protect consumer interests, the department conducts daily on-site monitoring of importers, producers, and sellers, and if any irregularities are found, immediate fines are imposed according to the Consumer Protection Act, 2075, and the monitoring report is made public daily through the department's website. It is also informed that the Nepal Oil Corporation has significantly reduced the price of petroleum products after the date this answer was sent. As honorable members are aware. Subsequently, airfare and transportation fare rates have also been adjusted. The ministry wishes to urge representatives of private sector organizations to adjust the prices of other goods. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable members, now the questioning honorable member... (12:49 PM) Honorable Minister, please wait a moment. As the honorable member wishes to ask a supplementary question, I provide time to ask a supplementary question focused on the topic. Honorable Mr. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Nepal Communist Party): - Honorable Chairperson, thank you for the answer. My supplementary question is as follows: You have admitted that intermediaries have an influence on price increases. What measures has the government adopted to prevent this? Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Minister. (12:50 PM) Honorable Minister of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Ms. Gauri Kumari: - We have activated the Commerce Department, and they are working through three channels daily. They are conducting inspections everywhere and making efforts to control prices. (12:50 PM) Honorable Chairperson: - Now I request the Honorable Minister to take his seat. Honorable members, I would like to inform you that the discussion on the appropriation titles of the Appropriation Bill, 2083, received with a message from the House of Representatives, will be answered by the concerned Honorable Ministers. Accordingly, today, the discussion on the appropriation titles related to the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Ministry of Agriculture, Forest and Environment, Ministry of Physical Infrastructure Development, Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Defense, Office of the President, Office of the Vice President, Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers, and the Secretariat of the National Planning Commission has been scheduled for the concerned ministers to answer the questions raised. Honorable members, if clarification is required regarding the answers of the concerned ministers for the appropriation titles, only those honorable members who participated in the discussion on the appropriation titles of the concerned ministry will be able to seek clarification. Honorable members, now I provide time to the Honorable Minister of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Ms. Gauri Kumari, to answer the questions raised during the discussion on the appropriation titles related to the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies. Honorable Minister of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Ms. Gauri Kumari: - Honorable Chairperson, greetings to all honorable members. I express my sincere gratitude for providing me with time in the esteemed house to answer the questions raised by the honorable members regarding the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies during the discussion on the allocated budget for the fiscal year 2083/084. The important statements, suggestions, and guidance expressed by the honorable members during the discussion on the allocated budget for the fiscal year 2083/084 have provided encouragement to the ministry to make its future performance effective and to facilitate the industrial and commercial environment. I would like to express my gratitude to the honorable members for their positive suggestions regarding the allocated budget and programs for the ministry and its subordinate bodies. The collective guidance of the honorable members has also inspired the implementation of the budget and programs through inter-ministerial coordination. The government has presented the budget for the upcoming fiscal year as a base year with the goal of achieving 7% annual economic growth, building an economy of 100 billion dollars in 5 years, creating more than 1.2 million jobs, and increasing domestic production and productivity. I wish to inform you that the budget and programs for this year have been presented with investment efficiency to achieve the goals set by the government using available resources.

Development, promotion, investment promotion of industry and business, concessions and facilities for domestic industries, collateral-free loans for youth with skills and readiness to bear risk, business development services, improvement of service delivery using digital technology, and other arrangements to increase domestic production and create employment, the government is sincerely committed to this. In this context, I would like to shed light before the esteemed House regarding the discussions on the allocated budget for the fiscal year 2083/084 and the questions raised by the honorable members during the discussion on the budget and programs. Seventeen honorable members presented their views on the budget discussion. All honorable members expressed their views focusing on production, employment, trade, entrepreneurship, supply management, revival of sick industries, and similar topics in one way or another. It has been expressed by the honorable members that there is a need to create a conducive production, investment, and business environment by coordinating and interconnecting various ministries of the Government of Nepal. I would like to pledge that the ministry will remain active in increasing production, productivity, and employment by further enhancing inter-ministerial and inter-level coordination and boosting the morale of the private sector. For this, the ministry is preparing investment protection and promotion and policy formulation, which is in the process of being approved by the Council of Ministers of the Government of Nepal. This strategy aims to establish private property protection, investment protection, and industries as peaceful sectors. The strategy also provides various concessions and facilities to re-operationalize industries that have been closed and become sick due to the damage caused during past movements. Under the Startup Entrepreneurship Loan Program targeting youth who wish to start businesses, I would like to inform you that loans are being processed for 966 projects in this fiscal year through collateral-free loans at subsidized interest rates. I would like to assure you that this program will be implemented more effectively in the coming fiscal year as well, and the ministry is also preparing an action plan for budget implementation to bring the allocated budget into implementation from the beginning of the fiscal year. Honorable Chairperson, some new programs have also been included in the programs for the upcoming fiscal year. Among these, a budget of 34 crore has been allocated for the National Enterprises Facilitator Program. Through its implementation, procedures are being formulated to make policy facilitation, program implementation, inter-agency and inter-level coordination, startup business activity services, and business promotion services more effective for micro, small, and medium enterprises and startups. Under the employment-linked production sector program, new industries will be established in the previously announced industrial areas with the objective of creating more employment by providing plots. The ministry has already started the process of managing and operating the industries located within 10 industrial areas established in various locations for the industrialization of the country. In this context, I would like to inform you that the Industrial Area Management Limited has started the process of collecting approximately 43 crore 46 lakh in outstanding land rent and providing land to actual productive industries to increase production and employment. Honorable Chairperson, I am now going to respond sequentially to the questions raised by the honorable members regarding the budget and programs of the Ministry of Industry, Commerce, and Supplies. The honorable members have raised suggestions and questions such as: Nepali products need to be branded and quality improved, tea export needs to be facilitated, export promotion and market diversification are needed, paddy needs to be purchased, export strategies need to be developed for goods like tea and cardamom, budget for startup loans needs to be increased, policies need to be made to create employment, establishment of organic fertilizer industry, promotion of SMEs, reduction of production costs, production of packaged organic jaggery, promotion programs for coffee, production of raw materials like hemp for the garment industry, operation of rural industries, reduction of trade deficit, renewal of TIPA agreement, smooth supply of petroleum products and establishment of an automatic pricing system, no value addition in processed exports, policies to achieve economic prosperity, industries in Biratnagar and elsewhere not running well, unemployment and lack of production due to closure, operation of Hetauda Garment Industry, need to operate existing industries rather than talk about them, no budget for petroleum exploration, export-oriented industries, green industries, promotion of PPP models, etc. Honorable Chairperson, I would like to express my commitment that the government is taking the issues raised by the honorable members seriously and implementing them with priority, and these issues will be further addressed through the budget and programs for the upcoming year. A task force has been formed to find a long-term solution to the problems seen in tea exports from Nepal to India, and its report is being prepared. Diplomatic efforts have also removed the existing obstacles, and smooth export arrangements have now been made. To solve the storage problem and expand market access for tea and cardamom, etc., resources have also been managed for the storage and warehouse construction of tea and cardamom with cost-sharing from the entrepreneurs in the concerned sector. The purchase and distribution of paddy and wheat at the minimum support price are being carried out through the Food Management and Trading Company Limited, and this has been prioritized in the budget for the upcoming fiscal year. Honorable Chairperson, the ministry has prioritized the work of developing commodity-specific export strategies and promoting exports for goods with export potential identified in the Nepal Trade Integration Strategy 2080. In this context, draft export strategies have already been prepared for three commodities: ginger, chupi, and carpets. In the upcoming fiscal year, export strategies will be developed and implemented for other commodities mentioned by the honorable members. In line with the government's policy to promote startups, the Startup Fast Track Action Plan, which includes 100-point agendas, has been approved and implemented, and a Startup Fast Track Help Desk has also been established at the Industrial Business Development Foundation. Furthermore, a significant amount of resources has been allocated within the available limit for the upcoming fiscal year to provide concessional loans to startup enterprises. Various programs for promoting entrepreneurship and skill development to create employment and self-employment opportunities within the country have been included in the budget for the upcoming year. Through programs such as women's entrepreneurship, business development centers, national entrepreneurship services, and youth entrepreneurship, encouragement, skills, and technology will be provided to those who wish to start businesses, I would like to inform the honorable members through the esteemed Chairperson. Honorable Chairperson, some honorable members raised the issue of lack of programs to reduce costs and promote SMEs, and the branding of organic products. In this regard, the Industrial and Trade Logistics Master Plan, prepared with the objective of reducing industrial and trade logistics costs and facilitating trade, has been approved and will be implemented with promptness. I also wish to inform you that the National Productivity Master Plan is being prepared to increase productivity in the industrial sector. Furthermore, to enhance the competitive capacity of productive industries through the annual budget, a concession on electricity tariffs has been provided by reviewing the demand charge for electricity, and the ministry is making efforts for special electricity tariffs for small and medium-sized industries. Programs are being operated through the Trade and Export Promotion Center for the packaging, marketing, and export promotion of Nepali organic products, and various programs have been proposed for the upcoming fiscal year. Regarding rural industries, the Government of Nepal has initiated the process of evaluating the assets and liabilities of seven government industries. Based on this study, the modality for operating the industries will be determined. I would like to inform you that industries in Biratnagar and other closed and sick industries across the country will be managed through a transparent process. A study report has been prepared for the re-operation of Hetauda Garment Industry, and cleaning, maintenance, and trial production are underway through the Directorate of Military Material Production. We are trying to operate it as a means to replace imports, develop self-reliance, create employment, and increase the contribution of the industrial sector to the economy. Honorable Chairperson, the government has formulated and is implementing an action plan with priority to reduce the trade deficit, and we have requested the US government to extend the period of duty-free, quota-free facilities under the Nepal-US trade agreement, which has expired. Despite the unfavorable situation created in West Asia, the supply management of petroleum products in Nepal has been effective. To protect consumer interests, daily market monitoring has been intensified by the Department of Commerce, Supply, and Consumer Protection in coordination with various agencies. During this period, a Price Transparency Week was also organized, which I would like to inform this House about. An investment express policy has been adopted to promote domestic investment and attract foreign investment. For this, a system for approving foreign investment entirely online has been adopted. This will reduce the time and cost for investors. All types of services are being gradually transformed into virtual mode from the One-Stop Service Center. Preliminary studies have confirmed a natural gas reserve of 112.1 billion cubic meters in the Jaljale area of Dailekh, creating a theoretical basis for producing 200 MW of electricity daily and 2200 tons of urea fertilizer and producing vehicle fuel through its use. The major challenges for this project include developing basic infrastructure such as roads, electricity, and drinking water required for commercial excavation and managing large-scale investment. In this context, I would like to inform you that we have a plan to proceed with the project in a phased and systematic manner by accelerating detailed technical and economic feasibility studies, prioritizing the implementation of work such as establishing a subsidiary of Nepal Oil Corporation to determine the investment modality, formulating sector-specific national standards, and collaborating with universities for technical manpower development. The work of managing resources will be done accordingly. Starting the project and changing to electric boilers and furnaces, cleaner production, green

and programs such as operating environmental management in industries, energy and climate change work. The policy and program to encourage EV charging at petrol pumps is requested to be noted. Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Members, I would like to express my commitment to take seriously the valuable suggestions and concerns provided by the Honorable Members after in-depth study of the budget and programs of the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies and its subordinate bodies, and to implement them effectively. Thank you. (13:08 hrs) Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Members, I will provide time to the Honorable Members who wish to seek clarification regarding the response given by the Honorable Minister of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Gauri Kumari. I have allocated 1 minute for each Honorable Member wishing to seek clarification. Honorable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota. Honorable Bishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson, through you, I did not see a proper response to the points I raised with the Minister of Industry. I had raised the issue of cannabis. Why was it not included in the policy to legalize cannabis, bring it under the legal framework, and develop it as an industry? And another point, coffee can be internationalized, not just nationalized. No information was provided about coffee either, for which I seek a response. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Goma Devi Timalsina. Honorable Goma Devi Timalsina (Communist Party of Nepal): Honorable Chairperson, although our Industry Minister has brought very good things with great effort today, I feel that some things are still lacking. Now, regarding the Hetauda Industrial Estate, the inspection was carried out. According to the inspection, it has been said that cleaning has been done. When will this industry start operating? And how much budget has been allocated for it? That also needs to be known, needs to be stated. How many public enterprises are there across the country? How many are closed? How many are operational? How many are waiting to be revived? How many need to be closed? (... Time expired.) Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Ram Kumari Jhankri. Honorable Ram Kumari Jhankri (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honorable Chairperson, through you, I would like to ask the Honorable Minister two or three questions. Specifically, regarding the operation of the Hetauda Textile Industry, I had heard about it in the priorities and principles of the policy, program, and budget. What is the modality of its operation? Similarly, the Gorakhkali Rubber Industry was also a subject mentioned in the priorities and principles of the policy, program, and budget. What has happened regarding its operation and what is its modality? Furthermore, there was talk of operating the Dhaubadi Iron Industry, which I saw somewhere in the policy and program. What is happening with that? On the other hand, since there are many ministries involved in the budget, I couldn't see much. However, in terms of reducing the trade deficit and creating a self-reliant economy, there was no contribution seen from the industry sector, only from commerce. There are many questions on these issues, but what is happening regarding these issues? I seek information. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Now, to provide clarification regarding the clarification sought by the Honorable Members, I will provide time to the Honorable Minister of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Gauri Kumari. Honorable Minister of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Gauri Kumari: Thank you. Yes. The responsibility of creating a local environment for products like coffee has been given to the local government under the micro-enterprise development program. All of that is being done through the DDI, which is currently with the Ministry of Finance. Based on the report that comes through the DDI, we are operating other rural industries. I have written to the Ministry of Finance for the release of 3.3 million rupees for the textile industry, which has now been released. It has reached the Hetauda industry, and the repair work has also progressed. I want to assure you that it will come into operation within a few months. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Members, the discussion on the appropriation bill related to the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies concludes here. (Honorable Minister, please take your seat.) Honorable Minister of Agriculture, Forests and Environment, Gita Chaudhary: Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Members, I would like to express my sincere gratitude to the Honorable Members for participating in the discussion on the appropriation bills related to the Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment and for providing valuable suggestions and raising questions. Honorable Chairperson, regarding the budget allocation for the Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment for the fiscal year 2083/084, Honorable Members have primarily raised questions and suggestions regarding the overall budget allocation for the ministry being low, the budget only covering large farmers, the status of chemical fertilizers, the budget allocation for fertilizer management, human-wildlife conflict management, damage to crops, regulation and management of subsidies, agricultural bills, facilitation of tea cultivation exports, climate change, watershed conservation, river system management, etc. Honorable Members have provided valuable suggestions regarding increasing the budget in the agricultural sector, ensuring easy availability of production materials such as fertilizers, seeds, and irrigation, expanding the access and scope of agricultural insurance, allocating sufficient budget for agricultural research programs, national agricultural modernization programs, subsidies for organic fertilizers, small-scale irrigation, promotion of organic and biological fertilizers, providing relief to farmers, effective implementation of minimum support prices, and promotion and export facilitation of tea and coffee cultivation. I express my sincere gratitude and seek permission to present my views on the queries raised by you. Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Members, I would like to inform you that a total of 73 billion 12 crore has been allocated for the ministry. For the upcoming fiscal year 2083/084, the major programs under the ministry include 32 billion 46 crore for chemical fertilizer supply, which is approximately 59 percent of the agricultural budget. I would like to inform you that 2 billion 19 crore has been allocated for agricultural insurance, 1 billion 50 crore for incentive grants to sugarcane farmers, 34 crore for subsidies for organic fertilizers, 2 billion 64 crore for agricultural research programs, 2 billion 62 crore for the National Agricultural Modernization Program, and 1 billion 53 crore for the Hill Fruits and Vegetables Development Project, 1 billion 45 crore for the High-Value Agricultural Commodities Development Project, 97 crore for the National Chure Conservation Project, 1 billion for the Climate Resilient Chure Program, and 88 crore for the Biodiversity and Watershed Management Program. Similarly, budget allocation has been made with special priority for human-wildlife conflict management and sustainable forest management programs. Honorable Members, a large portion of the overall budget in agriculture is spent on the import of chemical fertilizers, and this amount is increasing every year. It is clear that sustainable development in the agricultural sector is not possible unless we seriously focus on alternatives. Accordingly, the ministry is moving forward with necessary plans and programs. I would like to share my views on the issues of low budget allocation in the agricultural sector, the budget targeting large farmers, and the management of the agricultural subsidy distribution system. I would like to inform the Honorable Members that the ministry's budget and programs have been proposed within the allocated budget ceiling. The overall budget for the ministry appears to be somewhat reduced due to pressure on national resources. As the Honorable Members have pointed out, I share the same understanding that the budget allocation in the agricultural sector is not sufficient. However, I request that efforts have been made to formulate effective budgets and programs according to the available budget ceiling. Regarding the budget allocation in the agricultural sector, I would like to inform you that efforts and initiatives necessary for the development of the agricultural sector are being undertaken through the integrated efforts of the federal government, provincial governments, and local levels, due to the limited scope and structure of the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development. Honorable Members may have seen a lack of clarity regarding point no. 24 (a) in the budget statement for the upcoming year 2083/084, which states that the government will provide up to 40 percent incentive grants to farmers for initial capital investment of up to Rs. 2 crore for agricultural and livestock production. I would like to inform you that this mentioned program is a pilot program of the current government, and efforts are underway to prepare a modality for program implementation that allows participation of both small and large farmers, and the ministry is actively working to develop an appropriate modality for small farmers to invest by joining groups and for large investors to invest individually. In addition, budget has been allocated with continuity to programs and projects that have been in operation to provide agricultural facilities and concessions to small, medium, and large farmers. The ministry is making necessary efforts to make agricultural subsidy distribution transparent and effective. I would like to inform you that a task force has been formed to analyze and study the subsidies provided in the agricultural sector over the past 10 years, and necessary work is underway. More than 75 percent of the budget allocated for the agricultural sector under the ministry is expected to directly benefit small farmers. This includes providing fertilizer to more than 1.4 million farmers through more than 14,000 agricultural cooperatives annually, issuing more than 150,000 agricultural insurance policies, disbursing incentive grants to the accounts of more than 60,000 sugarcane farmers, expanding artificial insemination services to more than 700,000 livestock, providing approximately 60 million doses of vaccines, expanding the area of various crops, expanding the irrigated area through small-scale irrigation, promoting mechanization, and other programs that directly benefit small, medium, and large farmers. Due to limited resources, the budget for agricultural research programs and agricultural modernization has been proposed to be somewhat lower, but programs and activities have been proposed in a way that achieves the expected goals and objectives by prioritizing programs and activities. In the upcoming fiscal year, under the National Agricultural Modernization Program, budget has been allocated for activities targeting production and productivity increase, modernization, and commercialization in specific production areas through 21 super zones and 206 zones, and for the operation of 239 new pocket areas for various crops.

Regarding chemical fertilizer, seeds, irrigation availability, and budget and programs: For the supply of chemical fertilizer in the upcoming fiscal year 2083/084, an amount of 32 billion 460 million has been allocated. The action plan for the supply and management of fertilizer for the upcoming fiscal year has already been prepared. In the current fiscal year 2082/083, while a budget of Rs. 28 billion 820 million was allocated for the supply of chemical fertilizer, as of June 19, 2083, 458,000 metric tons of fertilizer have been imported, and including the previous year's stock, 412,000 metric tons of fertilizer have been sold and distributed. Thus, the required fertilizer for the paddy season appears to be readily available. To address complaints regarding the distribution and availability of chemical fertilizer, contact persons have been arranged at the Ministry of Agriculture, Provincial Ministries. Regarding the availability of seeds, improved seeds and quality seeds developed by the farms under the Nepal Agricultural Research Council and the Department of Agriculture have been provided to producers, seed producer groups, cooperatives, farmers, and private companies. The private sector has been made more responsible for seed production and management. To promote indigenous and local seeds, a budget and program have been arranged to provide subsidies for quality seeds to farmers in 153 local levels through digital technology. Regarding the expansion of irrigation facilities: The Ministry allocates budget for the construction and maintenance of small-scale irrigation structures through national projects and conditional grants. For conditional grants, approximately 160 million rupees have been allocated for the construction and expansion of small irrigation structures in 156 local levels. For national projects, a budget of 47 million rupees has been allocated for the construction and expansion of small irrigation structures. Through the Ministry of Energy, Irrigation, and Water Resources, it is expected that irrigation facilities will be easily available in the arable land of Madhesh, Lumbini, and Sudurpashchim provinces in the coming days from the large-scale irrigation projects under construction. Coordination is being done with the Ministry of Energy, Irrigation, and Water Resources for the expansion of the irrigation sector. The Ministry has initiated the process of amending the National Tea and Coffee Development Board Act, 2049, and the National Tea Policy, 2057. An agreement has been signed between the Nepal Agricultural Research Council and the National Tea and Coffee Development Board, prioritizing research work for the development of new tea varieties, soil testing, and pest and disease management. To facilitate tea exports smoothly, the Government of Nepal and the Ministry have taken necessary technical and diplomatic initiatives to solve the problems of tea exporters, and the issue of tea export has now been resolved. To further establish the national trademark 'Nepal Tea Quality from the Himalayas' for Nepali orthodox tea in the international market, the Board is conducting promotional programs in coordination with Nepali embassies abroad. Necessary coordination has been prioritized with the Ministry of Industry to enact laws for the geographical indication (GI) and intellectual property protection of tea. While orthodox tea produced in Nepal is gaining international recognition, cooperation has begun with the private sector to develop a national symbol for CTC tea that reflects its distinct identity and quality. Furthermore, to promote the branding of Nepali tea, the Ministry has prioritized the participation of tea entrepreneurs in international fairs through the joint efforts of the National Tea and Coffee Development Board and the private sector. Regarding the need to provide farmers with weather forecast information: To mitigate potential losses in the agriculture sector due to weather and disaster-related causes, an early warning system has been arranged through the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology. Regarding subsidies for organic fertilizer and promotion of organic farming: To discourage the increasing use of chemical fertilizers and promote organic farming, a budget of 350 million rupees has been proposed for federal organic fertilizer subsidies and 112.4 million rupees for provincial conditional grants. In addition, budget has been proposed for soil health improvement programs in 250 local levels, green manure promotion programs in 39 local levels, and organic agriculture promotion programs in 35 local levels. Coordination is being done with the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority and the provinces to collect details of damages in the agriculture sector due to disasters and provide relief to farmers through a one-door system. Necessary budget and programs have been arranged to develop capacity and implement pilot programs in cooperation with local and provincial levels for monkey control. I inform you that in the coming days, the Ministry will continue to implement necessary policies and programs with the objective of strengthening farmer security, protecting agricultural production, and promoting human-wildlife coexistence. I have also informed that local administrations have been activated to take legal action against cooperatives or dealers involved in misappropriation and malpractice in the distribution of subsidized fertilizer, and grievance officers have been appointed at the federal ministry and focal persons at the provincial ministries to hear complaints related to fertilizer. In recent years, the demand for chemical fertilizer in the country has been increasing significantly, and the use of farmyard manure, compost, and green manure in the soil has been decreasing drastically, leading to a significant increase in dependence on chemical fertilizers. Since chemical fertilizers are not produced domestically, dependence on the international market directly affects fertilizer prices and supply. We are all aware of the impact of the wars in Israel, Iran, and America on fertilizer production, supply, and prices. The government has been providing substantial subsidies to farmers for chemical fertilizers. Currently, the cost of 1 kg of urea is Rs. 85 and DAP is Rs. 167. Farmers receive 82 percent and 74 percent subsidy on these two fertilizers, respectively. Fluctuations in international market prices of fertilizer also lead to fluctuations in cost and subsidy percentages. A month ago, the price of urea fertilizer reached Rs. 160. As the demand and price of fertilizer increase, the government's financial burden and fiscal pressure also increase. Moreover, the excessive use of urea fertilizer and less use of phosphorus and potassium-based fertilizers lead to an imbalance in the use of chemical fertilizers, resulting in a decline in soil health and quality. The ministry is serious about this, and budget has been arranged for the upcoming fiscal year to operate programs in collaboration with all three tiers of government to improve soil health and promote organic farming. I would like to earnestly request all honorable members to take special initiative to educate and raise public awareness about the balanced use of chemical fertilizers and soil conservation. Honorable Chairperson, I would now like to seek permission to clarify the issue related to chemical fertilizers raised by the honorable Narayan Dutt Mishra. The Government of Nepal has designated the Agricultural Materials Company Limited and the Salt Trading Corporation Limited to purchase and distribute chemical fertilizers to farmers on subsidy. These fertilizer distributing companies prepare cost estimates and accept bids that are substantially effective in terms of minimum price in accordance with the procedures and processes stipulated by the Public Procurement Act, 2063, and the Public Procurement Regulations, 2064. The cost of every fertilizer purchase contract is estimated based on the rate. A question was also raised regarding whether the government purchased DAP fertilizer at a higher price. The Agricultural Materials Company invited bids for the purchase of 30,000 metric tons of DAP fertilizer on February 27, and on March 14, 2083, the estimated cost per kg was USD 1104.88, but the bid was accepted at USD 1101, which is 0.35 percent lower than the estimate. Furthermore, for the purchase of 30,000 metric tons of DAP fertilizer through G2G, a contract was signed on June 1, 2026, at USD 1102.18 per metric ton, which is 1.40 percent lower than the estimated cost of Rs. 1117.81. Therefore, since the fertilizer was purchased based on international market prices, the issue of whether it was expensive or cheap is not relevant. Regarding the question that India purchased the same fertilizer from the same supplier at USD 540 per metric ton, while Nepal purchased 900 metric tons, the fertilizer mentioned by the honorable questioner as purchased by India at USD 540 per metric ton may be urea fertilizer, not DAP. The Agricultural Materials Company accepted a bid from a company called Aditya Birla at a rate of USD 975 per metric ton, which is 0.46 percent lower than the estimated cost of USD 905.76 per metric ton for urea fertilizer on May 15, 2026. Information has been received that on April 15, 2006, the neighboring friendly country India accepted bids from suppliers including Aditya Birla for the purchase of 2.4 million metric tons of urea fertilizer, comprising 1.4 million metric tons at USD 935 per metric ton and 1 million metric tons at USD 959 per metric ton. Therefore, based on this fact, it does not appear that the company purchased urea fertilizer from India at USD 540 per metric ton at the right time. Regarding why there is such a large difference between Nepal's and India's purchase prices, the facts mentioned above do not show a significant difference between Nepal's and India's fertilizer purchase prices. Furthermore, the rate at which the Government of India purchases is the price at which it arrives at any port in India from a third country, while in Nepal, additional costs such as transportation costs for unloading the fertilizer from the ship, bagging, and transporting it by rail or truck to the distributor's warehouse, and advance income tax are added to that amount. Therefore, the price at which India purchases incurs an additional cost of USD 120 to USD 150 per metric ton. Was fair competition ensured in fertilizer procurement? The fertilizer procurement process by the Government of Nepal through fertilizer distributing companies is carried out in accordance with the prevailing Public Procurement Act, 2063, and Regulations, 2064, and other applicable economic laws and regulations. For this, the Public Procurement Monitoring Office under the Government of Nepal invites international bids through the e-GP system, and fertilizer suppliers can submit bids from anywhere in the world.

Because fertilizer is purchased, it is based on fair competition. In the past, 6-7 fertilizer supply companies used to participate in tenders, but due to Nepal's relatively small fertilizer market and multiple handling and logistic problems, currently 3 to 4 suppliers participate in the tender process. Therefore, I would like to inform the esteemed assembly that fertilizer is purchased in accordance with the existing procurement laws and regulations through competitive bidding. Regarding the question of whether to investigate the price difference of approximately double, as I have already stated, the fact is that the government has not purchased fertilizer at a price difference of double compared to India, and the contract has been made for purchasing fertilizer at a slightly lower price than India, so the facts and data are not as the honorable members have stated. I would like to request that if any collusion, corruption, or environment of malpractice is found during the purchase, the government will be resolute in investigating and taking action and maintaining good governance, without any bias or prejudice. On one hand, there is a severe shortage of fertilizer across the country, and on the other hand, fertilizer is being purchased at a high price, which means a limited amount of fertilizer will arrive. Regarding the daily fluctuations in international market prices of chemical fertilizers, their direct impact is also felt in Nepal, so the rates in every contract will vary. From the budget allocated for the purchase of chemical fertilizers, fertilizer distribution companies purchase chemical fertilizers by preparing annual procurement plans according to the annual supply plan approved by the ministry, and in contracts where the purchase price is high, more subsidy is spent, resulting in less fertilizer arriving. Recently, as the price of urea has decreased in the international market, the Agricultural Materials Company has approved a tender on Asar 10th for the purchase of 30,000 metric tons of urea fertilizer at USD 449.75 per metric ton. However, the government cannot shirk its responsibility by not purchasing fertilizer, claiming that the international market price is high. This year, the government has supplied and distributed the highest amount of fertilizer to date. I would like to assure this assembly that efforts are being made to bring even more fertilizer in the new fiscal year 2083/084 than this year. Furthermore, regarding the budget of the Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment for the upcoming fiscal year 2083/084, I hope that the suggestions provided by the honorable members will be helpful in the implementation of the ministry's budget and programs for the upcoming fiscal year, and I express my sincere gratitude to you all again. Thank you.
